_: EXAMPLE — NOT A VALID CLAIM. Every number below the sourced line is a DECLARED input and must be argued in public before it settles anything. Running the adapter against mainnet with this file REFUSES, and the refusal names exactly what a human still has to decide. That refusal is the point of the file.
_numeraire: Stake on mainnet is denominated in 17 different mints, so it is not summable without prices. Conversion floors, so a converted total is never larger than the truth — but a wrong price RATIO between two mints tilts the graph's shape, and no rounding rule protects against that.
_gamma: The buffer the market asserts: 10%. With psi = 0.1%, Theorem 1 bounds the cascade at 1.1% of total stake.
_mints: A SOL liquid-staking token only appreciates against SOL, so a floor of 1 SOL per token is conservative and needs NO oracle — it is declared from structure, not from a feed. The three above are that case. The remaining contributing mints are deliberately absent: some are LSTs nobody here has verified as such, and at least one (jtojtomepa8beP8AuQc6eXt5FriJwfFMwQx2v2f9mCL, JTO) is not an LST at all and has no structural floor, so it needs a real declared price. The adapter refuses until every contributing mint is present.
_ncns: Each NCN with an active edge needs { profit, alpha }. profit is pi_s, the value an attacker gets from corrupting it, in numeraire base units — the paper assumes these are given and calls estimating them an open research direction. alpha is the fraction of stake required to corrupt it, a property of that NCN's consensus protocol which Jito's registry does not record. Neither is invented here.
